story-overview.user-story: As a system, I want a background worker that polls and processes triggers, so that proactive messages are sent at the right times.
story-overview.description: Implement an Arq-based background worker that: - Polls agentic-memories for pending triggers every 30s (scheduled) and 60s (condition) - Claims triggers to prevent duplicate processing in multi-worker environments - Evaluates condition triggers (fast, no LLM) - Executes processing pipeline: gate check → wake-up agent → delivery → fire report - Handles errors gracefully without crashing - Reports execution metrics to agentic-memories via fire endpoint
story-overview.design-reference: See Proactive AI Architecture Design Document Section 8.3 (Worker Architecture) Location: /Users/ankit/dev/annie/docs/design/proactive-ai-architecture.md

criterion.title: Scheduled Trigger Polling
criterion.then: - Calls IntentsClient.get_pending(trigger_type="scheduled") - For each due trigger: 1. Claims via IntentsClient.claim_intent(id) 2. If 409 Conflict → Skip (already claimed) 3. If claimed → Pass to processing pipeline

criterion.title: Condition Trigger Polling
criterion.then: - Calls IntentsClient.get_pending(trigger_type="condition") - For each trigger: 1. Skip if in_cooldown flag is true 2. Claims via IntentsClient.claim_intent(id) 3. If 409 Conflict → Skip 4. Evaluates condition via evaluators (fast, no LLM) 5. If condition met → Pass to processing pipeline 6. If not met → Call fire_intent() with status="condition_not_met"

criterion.title: Processing Pipeline
criterion.then: Execute in order: 1. Subconscious gate check 2. Wake-up agent execution 3. Telegram delivery (if not skipped) 4. Fire report to agentic-memories (clears claim)

criterion.title: Fire Reporting
criterion.then: Calls IntentsClient.fire_intent() with IntentFireRequest: - status: success | failed | gate_blocked | condition_not_met - message_id: Telegram message ID (if sent) - message_preview: First 100 chars - trigger_data: Runtime data (price at fire time, etc.) - gate_result: Subconscious gate details (if blocked) - evaluation_ms: Condition evaluation time - generation_ms: LLM generation time - delivery_ms: Telegram delivery time - error_message: Error details (if failed)

criterion.title: Error Resilience
criterion.then: - Worker continues running (doesn't crash) - Failed trigger logged - Will retry on next poll cycle - Error logged to Langfuse

criterion.title: Worker Configuration
criterion.then: Configuration includes: - Cron job: scheduled polling every 30s - Cron job: condition polling every 60s - Redis connection from environment - Max concurrent jobs: 10 - Job timeout: 60s

pattern.name: Redis Connection Pattern
pattern.description: Standard pattern for async Redis client creation from environment config
pattern.code-sample:
import redis.asyncio as redis from api.config import get_config
# In __init__ or module-level setup: config = get_config() redis_host = config.get("REDIS_HOST", "redis") redis_port = int(config.get("REDIS_PORT", 6379))
self.redis_client = redis.Redis( host=redis_host, port=redis_port, db=0, decode_responses=True, socket_connect_timeout=5, socket_timeout=5 )
# For Arq worker: from arq.connections import RedisSettings
redis_settings = RedisSettings( host=redis_host, port=redis_port, database=0 )
pattern.notes: - All backend services use redis.asyncio for async Redis operations - Connection pooling built-in - Graceful degradation when Redis unavailable (see StateManager pattern) - Arq uses RedisSettings for worker configuration

pattern.name: Manager Class Pattern
pattern.description: Standard pattern for service manager classes with Redis backing
pattern.code-sample:
class MyManager: """Manager for X functionality."""
def __init__(self, redis_client: Optional[redis.Redis] = None): """Initialize with optional Redis client (for testing).""" if redis_client: self.redis_client = redis_client self._should_close = False else: config = get_config() redis_host = config.get("REDIS_HOST", "redis") redis_port = int(config.get("REDIS_PORT", 6379)) self.redis_client = redis.Redis( host=redis_host, port=redis_port, db=0, decode_responses=True, socket_connect_timeout=5, socket_timeout=5 ) self._should_close = True
self._is_healthy = True
async def __aenter__(self): """Async context manager entry.""" try: await self.check_health() except Exception: logger.warning("Redis unavailable, degraded mode") self._is_healthy = False return self
async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb): """Async context manager exit.""" if self._should_close and self.redis_client: await self.redis_client.close()
pattern.notes: - Support both injected and self-created Redis clients - Async context manager support (__aenter__, __aexit__) - Graceful degradation when Redis unavailable - Health checking on initialization

pattern.name: Langfuse Tracing Pattern
pattern.description: Standard pattern for tracing with Langfuse @observe decorator
pattern.code-sample:
try: from langfuse.decorators import observe LANGFUSE_AVAILABLE = True except ImportError: LANGFUSE_AVAILABLE = False def observe(**kwargs): def decorator(func): return func return decorator
# Trace-level function (top-level entry point) @observe(name="process_trigger", as_type="trace") async def process_trigger(trigger: dict): """Process a trigger through the pipeline.""" # Implementation pass
# Span-level function (nested operation) @observe(name="evaluate_condition", as_type="span") async def evaluate_condition(trigger: dict) -> bool: """Evaluate condition trigger.""" # Implementation pass
# Decorator automatically captures: # - Function inputs/outputs # - Duration # - Errors/exceptions # - Metadata (can add via extra params)
pattern.notes: - Use as_type="trace" for top-level entry points (worker poll functions) - Use as_type="span" for nested operations (evaluate, gate check, etc.) - Graceful fallback if Langfuse not available - Fire-and-forget: tracing failures never block application - Automatic input/output/error capture

pattern.name: Logging Pattern
pattern.code-sample:
from api.logging import get_logger
logger = get_logger(__name__)
# Simple log logger.info("Worker started")
# Log with context (structured) logger.info( "Trigger processed", extra={ "trigger_id": trigger["id"], "trigger_type": trigger["trigger_type"], "user_id": user_id, "status": "success", "duration_ms": duration_ms } )
# Error logging logger.error( "Failed to process trigger", extra={ "trigger_id": trigger["id"], "error": str(e), "error_type": type(e).__name__ } )
pattern.notes: - Always use get_logger(__name__) for logger creation - Use extra={} for structured context - Common fields: duration_ms, user_id, conversation_id, request_id - Sensitive values automatically masked (API keys, tokens) - JSON format in production, readable in dev

pattern.name: Environment Configuration Pattern
pattern.description: Standard pattern for loading and validating environment variables
pattern.code-sample:
from api.config import get_config
# Load configuration (cached, validated on first call) config = get_config()
# Access required variables (raises ValueError if missing) redis_host = config["REDIS_HOST"] redis_port = int(config["REDIS_PORT"])
# Access optional variables with defaults log_level = config.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO")
# Sensitive values are automatically masked in logs # Shows only first 4 and last 4 characters (e.g., "secr...2345")
pattern.notes: - Configuration validated once on application startup - Missing required variables raise ValueError - Sensitive variables (API keys, tokens) automatically masked - Use get_config() not direct os.getenv() for consistency

adding-new-service.description: Pattern for adding a new service to docker-compose.yml
adding-new-service.template: services: worker: build: context: ./backend dockerfile: Dockerfile.worker # New Dockerfile for worker container_name: annie-worker ports: - "${WORKER_DEBUG_PORT:-5681}:5681" # Debug port (optional) environment: - LOG_LEVEL=${LOG_LEVEL:-INFO} - ENVIRONMENT=${ENVIRONMENT:-dev} - REDIS_HOST=redis - REDIS_PORT=6379 - AGENTIC_MEMORIES_URL=${AGENTIC_MEMORIES_URL} - LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=${LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY} - LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=${LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY} - LANGFUSE_HOST=${LANGFUSE_HOST:-https://us.cloud.langfuse.com} extra_hosts: - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway" depends_on: redis: condition: service_healthy backend: condition: service_healthy # Worker needs backend modules healthcheck: test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import sys; sys.exit(0)"] interval: 30s timeout: 10s retries: 3 start_period: 30s volumes: - ./backend:/app networks: - annie-network restart: unless-stopped
adding-new-service.notes: - Worker shares backend code volume for module access - Depends on redis and backend (for shared modules) - Uses same network (annie-network) for inter-service communication - Health check keeps worker alive - restart: unless-stopped ensures resilience

# Use in worker functions: async def poll_scheduled_triggers(ctx): client = IntentsClient() pending = await client.get_pending(trigger_type="scheduled") for trigger in pending: await process_trigger(trigger)
async def process_trigger(trigger: dict): """Full processing pipeline.""" user_id = trigger["user_id"]
# 1. Gate check gate_result = await check_subconscious_gate(user_id) if not gate_result.allowed: await report_fire(trigger, status="gate_blocked") return
# 2. Wake-up agent result = await wake_up_agent(trigger, user_id) if result.skip: await report_fire(trigger, status="skipped") return
# 3. Deliver message_id = await deliver_to_telegram(user_id, result.message)
# 4. Report await report_fire(trigger, status="success", message_id=message_id)

arq-worker-specifics.basic-worker-structure:
# backend/api/proactive/worker.py
from arq import cron from arq.connections import RedisSettings import os
async def poll_scheduled_triggers(ctx): """Poll for due scheduled triggers. Runs every 30 seconds.""" # ctx is the worker context (has redis pool, etc.) # Implementation here pass
async def poll_condition_triggers(ctx): """Evaluate condition triggers. Runs every minute.""" # Implementation here pass
class WorkerSettings: """Arq worker configuration."""
# Functions available to the worker functions = [poll_scheduled_triggers, poll_condition_triggers]
# Cron jobs (scheduled execution) cron_jobs = [ cron(poll_scheduled_triggers, second={0, 30}), # Every 30 seconds cron(poll_condition_triggers, minute=set(range(60))), # Every minute ]
# Redis connection redis_settings = RedisSettings( host=os.getenv("REDIS_HOST", "redis"), port=int(os.getenv("REDIS_PORT", 6379)), database=0 )
# Worker limits max_jobs = 10 # Max concurrent jobs job_timeout = 60 # Job timeout in seconds
# Logging log_level = os.getenv("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO")

decision.title: Claims-Based Multi-Worker Safety
decision.rationale: Uses agentic-memories Epic 6 Story 6.3 claims API with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to prevent duplicate processing. Worker claims trigger before processing, 409 Conflict indicates another worker already claimed it.
decision.implication: Safe to run multiple workers for high availability and scale.

decision.title: Separate Polling for Scheduled vs Condition
decision.rationale: Scheduled triggers need frequent polling (30s) for timely delivery. Condition triggers can poll less frequently (60s) since they're event-driven.
decision.implication: Two separate cron jobs with different intervals.

decision.title: Graceful Degradation on Errors
decision.rationale: Worker should never crash from a single trigger failure. Each trigger processed independently with try/except. Failed triggers will retry on next poll cycle.
decision.implication: Worker is resilient but may have delayed processing on errors.

decision.title: Stub Implementations for Dependencies
decision.rationale: Story 13.7 focuses on worker infrastructure and polling logic. Gate check, wake-up agent, and delivery are implemented in other stories. Use stubs/placeholders initially to test worker independently.
decision.implication: Full integration testing deferred to Story 13.11.

decision.title: Fire Reporting with Rich Metrics
decision.rationale: Fire report includes execution timing (evaluation_ms, generation_ms, delivery_ms), status, message preview, and error details. Enables observability and debugging.
decision.implication: Need to track timing for each pipeline phase.
